# Roadmap pruning

A roadmap, like an orchard, needs pruning every year. Ideas that nobody has mentioned for half a year are dead wood: they appear in every planning meeting and compete with the work that bears fruit. Cutting back is uncomfortable, yet it lets the team's vigour go to the few branches that matter.

The rule I follow: every quarter I walk through the roadmap and delete what is older than six months with no owner and no customer. The remaining items get more room. Pruning protects the schedule too, because a smaller scope is easier to finish.

Cut back early, and cut hard, instead of late and in panic.
